life_summary: Hyrum Smith was born February 9, 1800, in Tunbridge, Vermont, to Joseph Smith Sr. and Lucy Mack Smith. He was the eldest brother of Joseph Smith Jr. and grew up in a family of modest means. Between ages twelve and fifteen, Hyrum attended Moor's Charity School on the campus of Dartmouth College in Lebanon, New Hampshire, gaining education unusual for his social class. He was baptized in 1829 and became one of the Eight Witnesses, testifying to the reality of the golden plates. Hyrum married and had eight children, establishing himself as a committed member of his brother's new religious movement. His combination of family loyalty, spiritual commitment, and ecclesiastical responsibility made him one of Joseph's closest and most trusted advisors throughout the founder's ministry.
church_summary: Hyrum Smith was baptized in 1829 and became one of the Eight Witnesses to the Book of Mormon plates. When the church formally organized in 1830, he was the oldest charter member at age thirty. He served as a branch presiding officer and missionary, later becoming the church's Presiding Patriarch and Assistant President of the Church. Hyrum traveled with Joseph to Carthage, Illinois, in 1844 to face riot and treason charges. On June 27, 1844, during a mob attack on the jail, Hyrum was shot in the face and then struck again, declaring "I am a dead man" before his death. By 2000, estimates suggested over thirty-one thousand living descendants from his line.
